thread:
Tom (PM): kicking off a lightweight playbook for Dedicated capacity contracts. want to make sure launch criteria and default autoscale/ burst rules are clear for sales + solutions.
Elaine (Eng): sounds good. what's the minimum viable on policy surface? pretty sure we need min/max GPUs, burst window, and a backstop quota.
Tom (PM): minimal: reserved pool size, burst buffer (short-lived extra GPUs), per-customer monthly quota, and an autoscale cooldown. also SLA tier mapping.
Jasper (SRE): agree. add explicit preemption rules for lower tiers and a fallback to hosted models when preempted. that reduces customer outage blast radius.
Maria (CSE): customers keep asking for predictable tail-latency under heavy demos. how do we measure "predictable" in the contract?
Tom (PM): propose: 95th token latency <= X ms for standard tier, and uptime >= 99.9% for reserved pools. include a cost-protection clause for burst credit windows.
Elaine (Eng): can we make burst credits time-boxed (e.g., 30s buckets) and limited per-day? simpler to implement than arbitrary recharge schedules.
Jasper (SRE): +1. also prefer a soft-then-hard quota model: soft allows burst until credits exhausted, then hard throttle or fallback.
Tom (PM): draft suggested defaults (open for bikeshedding): reserved_gpus: 4, burst_credits: 60 GPU-seconds per minute (equiv to 1 extra GPU for 60s), daily_burst_cap: 3x baseline, autoscale_cooldown: 300s.
Elaine (Eng): posting a quick config sample — use as a spec for eng and infra:

```
policy:
  reserved_gpus: 4
  burst_pool_gpu_seconds_per_min: 60
  daily_burst_multiplier: 3
  autoscale:
    min_gpus: 1
    max_gpus: 8
    target_rps_per_gpu: 120
    cooldown_s: 300
    preemption_policy: "soft_then_hard"
```

Jasper (SRE): needs metrics hooks: token latency histogram, queue depth, and burst credit burn rate exposed at 1s granularity for console graphs.
Maria (CSE): for sales contracts, we should provide two templates: (1) demo-friendly (short high-burst with lower cost) and (2) steady-production (larger reserved pool, smaller burst).
Tom (PM): agreed. launch criteria checklist draft: public docs + examples, console UI for pool sizing, rollout text for sales, infra e2e test for preemption + fallback, SLA language reviewed by legal.
Elaine (Eng): estimate for MVP work: infra changes (4 wks), runtime gating + metrics (3 wks), console UX (2 wks), legal & contract templates (1 wk parallel). can try to parallelize.
Jasper (SRE): I'll scope the infra changes and add a small simulator to validate burst-window behavior under noisy neighbors.
Maria (CSE): I'll craft the two customer-facing templates and get early feedback from two pilot accounts.
Tom (PM): next steps: Elaine/Jasper — sync and drop a short RFC by EOW with the config format and migration plan. Maria — pilot list + contract snippets. I'll own rollout comms.
Elaine (Eng): acked, putting a stub RFC in #docs by tomorrow. @autoscale-bot can you run a sanity sim for the config above when ready?
autoscale-bot: scheduled simulation queued with policy id playbook-1781123456. estimated run 30m. will post results in channel when done. :gear:
Jasper (SRE): thanks — if sim shows >10% tail degradation we need to tighten the burst limits before shipping.
Tom (PM): good guardrail. closing loop: we'll iterate RFC -> pilot -> GA. keeping scope MVP minimal. any objections?
Maria (CSE): none. excited to get clearer contracts for customers.
Elaine (Eng): no objections. will include a migration path for existing dedicated customers.
Jasper (SRE): no objections. adding a postmortem template to capture weird edge cases during pilots.
Tom (PM): thanks everyone — filing this thread into the product roadmap doc and tagging action owners. :thumbsup:
